one_month_reasoning: The window contains Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-28 (pre-market), so the month carries an earnings-sized move. Orders should be strong: at the Morgan Stanley conference on 2026-10-01 the CEO pulled the $200B backlog milestone to very early 2027 and called the 20 GW 2H gas guide likely conservative (stock +3.9% that day to $987.45). Against that: Q2 EPS missed badly ($2.47 vs ~$3.2) and the stock fell on the print; EPS consensus for Q3 is scattered ($3.01-$4.15), EBITDA ~$1.7B; 1H26 FCF was already $9.9B of the $11.5-12.5B guide, so 2H FCF looks weak and any early 2027 framework could show the down-payment unwind; Wind losses persist. Credit (Fitch A-), insider selling (~$11.5M YTD) and litigation (Vineyard Wind settled 2026-09-16) give no near-term bear catalyst. Net: no directional edge; median ~$990 with ~15% monthly vol (52%/3.5), symmetric in log space.

fair_value.method: Blend of 30x 2028E EPS $31.50 = $945 (40%), 24x haircut 2028E EBITDA $10.2B plus ~$9B net cash over 260M shares = $977 (35%), and a 3.5% yield on ~$8.5B normalised FCF = $934 (25%); weighted ~$953, about 3% below the $987.45 close.

bear.story: GLJ-style outcome: 2026 proves the order peak (WoodMac), 2027-28 deliveries carry older-vintage pricing so EBITDA lands ~$8B in 2027, FCF falls toward management's cumulative floor (>=$8.3B for 2027-28 combined) as down payments unwind, data-center delays (30-50% of 2026 capacity slipping) or a hyperscaler capex growth stall dent Electrification, Wind keeps losing money; multiple compresses to ~20x EPS of ~$29. Not a balance-sheet or fraud story: credit is A-, insider selling is token.

base.story: Orders stay strong (backlog >$200B early 2027, 125+ GW gas under contract), margins expand toward management's 20% 2028 target, but the stock de-rates from ~40x to ~30x forward as order growth decelerates and FCF normalises; EPS growth roughly offsets de-rating for a mid-single-digit gain.

bull.story: AI power supercycle persists (all hyperscalers raised or reaffirmed 2026 capex in September), pricing on 2025-26 vintage backlog drives Power margins above 20%, Wind turns, services backlog compounds to ~$100B; multiple holds ~38x on ~$38 2028 EPS (Guggenheim $1,450 street high).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$640 (-35%, ~20x 2028E EPS and near the lower part of the 52-week range) the move would most likely reflect a fundamental break: slot reservations failing to convert or being cancelled, a hyperscaler capex pullback hitting Electrification and gas orders, or evidence that 2027 Power margins are as thin as GLJ argues, rather than ordinary 52%-vol noise. Credit, litigation and insider activity are not plausible break triggers on current evidence.

reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with the search budget restored. Verified facts: Q2 2026 orders $24.2B (+88% organic), backlog $176B, FY26 guide revenue $45.5-46.5B, FCF $11.5-12.5B (1H already $9.9B), cash $13.1B, total debt $3.72B (net cash ~$9.0B, not the ~$12B I estimated), ~263M diluted shares. Skeptic-lane checks now done directly: Fitch upgraded to A- on 2026-08-12 (leverage just over 1x) and 2026 notes priced at +45-78bp, so credit is a non-issue; Form 4 data show only ~$11.5M of 2026 open-market insider sales and no buys, routine for a $263B company; short interest 3.3%; Vineyard Wind's $853M claim was settled 2026-09-16 (terms undisclosed); no short-seller report beyond GLJ's Sell and no accounting red flag found. The real bear case is earnings-quality and cyclicality: contract liabilities rose $14.1B in 1H26, so 2026 FCF is pulled forward and management's cumulative 2025-28 FCF floor (>=$24B) implies a sharp 2027-28 FCF step-down; consensus 2028 revenue ($61B) already exceeds management's $56B outlook; WoodMac sees 2026 as peak orders; GLJ sees 2030-31 oversupply. Offsetting: every hyperscaler raised or held 2026 capex in September, Polymarket prices only 9% US recession odds by end-2026 ($2.2M volume, read 2026-10-01), and the CEO says 2032 slots are selling. Revised methods (P/E 30x on $31.50 2028E = $945, EV/EBITDA 24x on $10.2B + $9B net cash = $977, 3.5% FCF yield on $8.5B = $934) give ~$953 vs $972 before; scenario mean ~$1,041 (+5%). Ladder: lognormal median ~$1,005 with ~47% vol (below the 52% realized as a mega-cap), left tail kept slightly fat for de-rating risk but trimmed a little versus round 1 because credit, litigation and insider-selling risks are now verified as small. Street mean target $1,237 (37 analysts) treated as evidence of optimism, not the answer. Twelve Data estimate and Alpha Vantage endpoints were unavailable (plan limits/rate limit), so consensus came from aggregator pages; TheStreet and some Seeking Alpha news pages blocked fetching.
